blocks.text: Zscaler Endpoint Context uses extensive application data that it collects from Zscaler Client Connector to provide the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE) with additional endpoint-related telemetry to add to existing identity, network, and cloud telemetry already available. The Zscaler service builds an inventory of commonly abused OS and all non-OS applications residing on each endpoint, both actively running and at rest, and enumerates a rich data set related to each application. This rich data enables you to have a complete end-to-end view of activity across your organization, starting with applications on the endpoints themselves.

Extensive endpoint application metadata is now available for use as criteria in policy, allowing the policies to be effectively application-aware, allowing for greater flexibility and the ability to dictate behavior of policies based on the source endpoint application, a list of endpoint applications, or the risk associated with the endpoint application from the risk-quantification process. Additionally, Endpoint Context benefits all Internet & SaaS customers, regardless of licensing, by providing additional endpoint application and process metadata for inclusion in threat detection engines. To learn more see Configuring the Firewall Filtering Policy, Configuring the DNS Control Policy, and Configuring SSL/TLS Inspection Policy.
Endpoint Context provides the following benefits and allows you to:

blocks.item: Monitor application usage on endpoints across your organization.
See commonly abused applications on each endpoint.
Have end-to-end visibility of endpoint applications across your organization.

blocks.text: On the Application Investigation page (Cyberthreat Protection > Policy > Endpoint Context), you can view the following pages:

blocks.item: Overview Page
On the Overview page, you can do the following:
Go to the Inventory Page.
See the list of detected applications by OS.
See the certificate status for all detected endpoint applications.
See the instances of applications sorted by threat type.

See a list of the top application versions with vulnerabilities. You can filter the list by vulnerability level (i.e., critical, high, medium, and low). You can also click application names to see more detailed information:
See image.
See the top applications by category (e.g., AI Assistance, Browsers, File Sharing). You can click application names to see more detailed information.
See the top applications by threat category (e.g., malicious, suspicious). You can click application names to see more detailed information.
See the top applications with a custom certificate trust store. You can click application names to see more detailed information.
See the top applications installed on endpoints across your organization. You can click application names to see more detailed information.
See the list of top AI applications. You can click application names to see more detailed information.
Inventory Page
On the Inventory page, you can do the following:
Go to the Overview Page.
Filter the application information on the page, and add or remove filters to control the information you see.
See the total number of detected applications by OS.
See the instances of applications sorted by threat type.
See the certificate status for all detected endpoint applications.
View a list of all detected applications for your organization. For applications, you can see the following:
Application Name: The name of the application installed on endpoints. You can sort this column.
Product Name: The product name of the application. You can sort this column.
Last Execution: The last time an executable was run on an endpoint. You can sort this column.
Code Signing: The certificate status for the application.
Category: The category of the application.
Distinct Versions: The number of distinct versions of the application running on endpoints across your organization.
Instances: The number of instances of the application running on endpoints across your organization.
Threat Type: The threat type for the application (i.e., malicious, suspicious, benign, unknown).
Vulnerabilities: The vulnerabilities by the CVE severity level of the application (i.e., critical, high, medium, low).
Add or remove columns from the table.
Specify the number of rows available in the table.
